recognize_zh: 視野下方一顆小型淋巴球，核深染並有細密交錯的溝紋，呈腦迴狀，幾乎看不到胞質；左上角的中性球可作為大小與顆粒胞質的對照，典型小型 Sézary 細胞。
features: Small lymphoid cell about the size of a red cell with a very high N:C ratio
Nucleus with multiple fine grooves producing a cerebriform (brain-like) pattern
Dense hyperchromatic chromatin without visible nucleoli
Normal segmented neutrophil at upper left; red cells include occasional target and stomatocyte-like forms
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small lymphoid cell with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, dense hyperchromatic chromatin, and a finely grooved cerebriform nucleus without visible nucleoli. A normal segmented neutrophil is present for comparison. Red cells show occasional target and stomatocyte-like forms, and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with a small Sezary cell; quantitation by flow cytometry is required for a diagnosis of Sezary syndrome.

ddx.vs: Normal lymphocytes have a round nucleus with smooth contour and at most a single shallow indentation, not multiple fine convoluted grooves.
CLL cells have round nuclei with coarse clumped soccer-ball chromatin and are CD5/CD23-positive B cells.
Benign erythroderma may have occasional cerebriform cells, so diagnosis requires a clonal CD4-positive population with CD7 or CD26 loss.
